title: Coefficient and site squares for the explicit refinement theta
statement:
Let $X,T_1,T_2$ be Noetherian schemes [def-pc-scheme], meaning schemes admitting finite affine covers by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $u:T_1\to T_2$ be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] and $j_a:X\hookrightarrow T_a$ open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion] with $uj_1=j_2$. Use the constant-ring module derived categories on the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. For every finite commutative ring $R$, form $V=T_1\times_{T_2}X$ with $b:V\to T_1$, $p:V\to X$, and the open-and-closed section $s=(j_1,1_X):X\to V$. Let
$$\theta_{u,R}=c_{p,s,R}\circ Rp_{*,R}(e_{u,R})\circ r_{u,R}:j_2^*Ru_{*,R}j_{1!}\xrightarrow{\sim}1$$
be the specified composite of open restriction $r_u$, open base-change $e_u:b^*j_{1!}\cong s_!$, and component restriction $c_{p,s}:Rp_*s_!\cong1$ in [def-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison, lem-weil-pbc-derived-open-restriction, lem-weil-pbc-clopen-section-direct-image]. Let $\alpha_{u,R}:j_{2!}\to Ru_{*,R}j_{1!}$ be the open adjunct of $\theta_{u,R}^{-1}$ specified there.

Let $A\to B$ be a unital map of finite commutative rings and set $T_T=-\otimes^L_{A_T}B_T$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Let $t_a:T a_{!,A}\cong a_{!,B}T$ be the summandwise open tensor map, and $q_u:T Ru_{*,A}\to Ru_{*,B}T$ the $B$-linear adjoint transpose of the $A$-counit after coefficient extension, using the canonical pullback/tensor comparison. For every $L\in D^+(X_{\rm et},A)$ with $L_B\in D^+(X_{\rm et},B)$,
$$Ru_{*,B}(t_{j_1}(L))\circ q_u(j_{1!,A}L)\circ T_{T_2}(\alpha_{u,A}(L))
=\alpha_{u,B}(L_B)\circ t_{j_2}(L).$$
This is an equality in the unbounded category, without asserting $T(D^+)\subseteq D^+$.

For a finite commutative $R$ write $N_T=\nu_T^*$, $e_j:N j_!^{\rm et}\cong j_!^{\rm pro}N$ for the canonical open comparison [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison], and $d_u:N Ru_*^{\rm et}\cong Ru_*^{\rm pro}N$ for the counit mate [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate]. Define $\theta_{u,R}^{\rm pro}$ on etale-origin bounded-below input by the same three constituents: the site-transported open-restriction exchange, the summandwise open base-change identification, and restriction to the clopen component. Let $\alpha_{u,R}^{\rm pro}$ be the open adjunct of its inverse. Then for every $L\in D^+(X_{\rm et},R)$,
$$Ru_{*,R}^{\rm pro}(e_{j_1}(L))\circ d_u(j_{1!}^{\rm et}L)\circ N_{T_2}(\alpha_{u,R}(L))
=\alpha_{u,R}^{\rm pro}(N_XL)\circ e_{j_2}(L).$$
Both equations are natural in $L$ and require no cartesian hypothesis on the original refinement square and no flatness hypothesis on $B$ over $A$.

source.place: Tag 0F7B (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open), specialized to a refinement, with the theta_u construction specified in def-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison. Agent-stated naturality of the three constituents under coefficient and site change.

proof.text: First identify the coefficient maps with the normalizations in [lem-sf-proper-open-coefficient-refinement]. Its $Q$ is our $T$, its $\lambda_u:u_B^*T\cong Tu_A^*$ is the same canonical pullback/tensor comparison, and its $\chi_u$ is $q_u$: their $B$-linear transposes are both $T(\varepsilon_{u,A})\lambda_u$. Its $\beta_j$ is $t_j$. Indeed, before deriving, the summandwise tensor map restricted to the open sends $m\otimes b$ to the same tensor; under the open unit it is the identity. Its inverse therefore has open-adjunction transpose $\lambda_{j,j_!M}^{-1}T(\eta_{j,A,M})$, exactly the formula specifying $\beta_j$. This check also holds on K-flat representatives and hence after localization, by [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. It is a check of $B$-linear maps, not of their underlying $A$-linear maps.

source.place: Tag 0E8I, lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor; the identity on the open, with derived descent as in Tag 0GL1

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-proper-open-coefficient-refinement] with $K=L$. Its hypotheses are exactly the present proper refinement of Noetherian schemes, the unital map of finite commutative rings, $L\in D^+(A)$ and $T_XL=L_B\in D^+(B)$. Its $\alpha_{u,R}$ uses the same specified three-factor $\theta_{u,R}$, including component restriction. Substituting the identifications in Step 1 into its displayed equation gives the coefficient equation of this item in $D(T_{2,\mathrm{et}},B)$. In particular no claim that $T$ preserves $D^+$ and no invertibility of $q_u$ on arbitrary input is used.

source.place: Tag 0GL6, remark-Rf-lower-shriek-change-of-rings; the named-map refinement is the existing cited node, not an additional assertion attributed to the remark

proof.text: For the site equation fix $R$ and suppress it in notation. Write superscripts $e,p$ for the etale and pro-etale functors. By [lem-weil-pbc-proper-open-section], $b$ is open, $s$ is clopen and $ps=1_X$; by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-open-p-proper], $p$ is proper. Thus the direct-image mate comparison applies to both proper maps $u,p$ (proper morphisms are quasi-compact and separated, hence quasi-separated). Put $K=j^e_{1!}L$. Exactness of etale open extension and inverse image, together with [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-bounded-below], gives $K,b_e^*K,s^*b_e^*K\in D^+$. By [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact], every $N$ here is additive and exact, carries the constant ring to the same constant ring, and preserves these lower bounds. These facts type every occurrence of $d_u,d_p$ below on bounded-below etale input.

source.place: Tag 099R, section-comparison; proper/open geometry of the specified theta construction

proof.text: Let $Z=V\setminus s(X)$. We will use the two components $V=s(X)\amalg Z$ to test maps, without testing derived maps on stalks. On the etale site [lem-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-clopen-product] gives the product description of abelian sheaves and their morphisms. An $R$-action is a family of component actions, so the same description holds for $R$-module sheaves. On the pro-etale site the module version and the insertion $s_!M=(M,0)$ are [lem-sp-clopen-section-component]. These exact inverse equivalences extend to complexes and their homotopies componentwise. Quasi-isomorphisms are componentwise; the two inverse functors and their unit identities therefore descend by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]. Consequently in each derived category a map into $s_!M$ is determined by its $s^*$ restriction: in the product it is a pair $(f,0)$. Also $s_!$ is right adjoint to $s^*$ with unit the projection $F\to s_!s^*F$.

source.place: Disjoint-open-cover product description; componentwise extension to complexes and localization written out

proof.text:
Write $a_v:N_{\mathrm{src}(v)}v_e^*\xrightarrow{\sim}v_p^*N_{\mathrm{tgt}(v)}$ for [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]. It is coherent for composites and the cartesian square defining $V$. Write $E_a:N a^e_!\xrightarrow{\sim}a^p_!N$ for [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison], reserving $e^e,e^p$ for the open base-change constituent of $\theta$. The $E_a$ preserve the normalized open unit: the comparison identifies the same section over an object in the open, and extension by zero inserts zero otherwise; exactness lets this identity pass termwise to complexes. For the square $(1_X,s,j_1,b)$ this gives
$$E_s(L)N_V(e^e_L)=e^p_{N_XL}\,b_p^*(E_{j_1}(L))\,a_{b,K}.\tag{O}$$
To check the equation, use the inverse-open-unit description of etale base change in [lem-cbc-extension-zero-base-change], and the pro-etale unit normalization in [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization] applied to $g=b,j=j_1$. Both sides land in $s^p_!N_XL$, and their sources are supported on $s(X)$ by the canonical open base-change isomorphisms. Restricting to $s(X)$ makes both maps the identity on $N_XL$, by coherence of $a$ and the preceding unit identity. Full faithfulness of pro-etale open extension, stated in that normalization node, proves (O).

source.place: Tag 09AF, lemma-jshriek-comparison, adjoint comparison; canonical open-unit normalization

proof.text:
The open-restriction constituent obeys the following mate identity on $K$:
$$r^p_{N_{T_1}K}\,(j_2^p)^*d_u(K)\,a_{j_2,Ru_*^eK}
=Rp_*^p(a_{b,K})\,d_p(b_e^*K)\,N_X(r^e_K).\tag{R}$$
Here $r^e$ is open restriction [lem-weil-pbc-derived-open-restriction], with its canonical exchange normalization, and $r^p$ is the site-transported open restriction of the statement. To verify the named maps in (R), express restriction exchange as the adjoint of $b^*\varepsilon_u$ after the inverse-image square, exactly the formula of [def-kun-unbounded-exchange]. Express $d_u$ and $d_p$ by the counit equations of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate]. The two pastings of inverse-image comparisons are equal because [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] is compatible with the cartesian identification and composites. Taking their mates by clauses (1),(2) of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] gives the two composites displayed in (R), with these orientations. This uses the normalization of $d$, not an unspecified isomorphism of the two direct images.

source.place: Tag 07A7, remark-base-change; Tags 0E46 and 0E47, pasting of exchange mates

proof.text:
Write $c^e:Rp_*^es^e_!L\xrightarrow{\sim}L$ for [lem-weil-pbc-clopen-section-direct-image] and $c^p:Rp_*^ps^p_!N_XL\xrightarrow{\sim}N_XL$ for component restriction on the pro-etale side. The latter is computed termwise by [lem-sp-clopen-section-component], whose insertion preserves K-injectives. The inverse of either $c$ has proper-adjunction transpose
$$\rho^\bullet:p_\bullet^*M\longrightarrow s^\bullet_!M,$$
the clopen projection, using $s^*p^*M=M$. Indeed $s^*\dashv s_!$ is the projection/insertion adjunction of Step 4, so its unit is $(1,0)$. The composite $s^*p^*\dashv Rp_*s_!$ has left functor the identity and counit precisely restriction of sections to the component, which is the specified $c$. The composite hom bijection of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] therefore takes $c^{-1}$ to the identity under $s^*p^*=1$ and, before the last transpose, to the projection $\rho$. This proves the normalization on both sites, not just existence of an isomorphism $Rp_*s_!\cong1$.

source.place: Component section formula; composite hom bijection and clopen projection normalization

proof.text:
Exact additive $N_V$ preserves the clopen projection. More explicitly, with $M=L$ on the etale side and $M=N_XL$ on the pro-etale side, the map
$$E_s(L)\,N_V(\rho^e_L)\,a_{p,L}^{-1}:p_p^*N_XL\longrightarrow s^p_!N_XL$$
has restriction $1_{N_XL}$ on $s(X)$: $ps=1_X$, compatibility of $a$ with composites, and the unit normalization of $E_s$ in Step 5 identify all factors there with the identity. Its complementary component is zero, since its target has zero complementary component. By Step 4 it is $\rho^p_{N_XL}$. This is an equality in the module derived category, obtained from the product equivalence; no faithfulness of stalks or of a restriction-of-scalars functor is asserted.

source.place: Tag 09AF open comparison, restricted to a clopen component; component calculation

proof.text:
Now form
$$h=Rp_*^p(E_s(L))\,d_p(s^e_!L)\,N_X((c^e)^{-1}):N_XL\longrightarrow Rp_*^ps^p_!N_XL.$$
Its transpose under $p_p^*\dashv Rp_*^p$, by the counit normalization of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate] and naturality of $a_p$, is
$$E_s(L)\,N_V\bigl(\varepsilon^e_{p,s_!L}\,p_e^*((c^e)^{-1})\bigr)\,a_{p,L}^{-1}
=E_s(L)N_V(\rho^e_L)a_{p,L}^{-1}=\rho^p_{N_XL}.$$
The first equality uses the transpose identified in Step 7, and the last equality is Step 8. The hom bijection [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] makes $h=(c^p)^{-1}$. Multiplying by $c^p$ on the left and by $N_X(c^e)$ on the right gives
$$c^p\,Rp_*^p(E_s(L))\,d_p(s^e_!L)=N_X(c^e).\tag{C}$$

source.place: Tag 0B65, lemma-transformation-between-functors-and-adjoints: counit normalization; explicit transpose calculation

proof.text:
Define
$$C_L=(j_2^p)^*Ru_*^p(E_{j_1}(L))\,(j_2^p)^*d_u(K)\,a_{j_2,Ru_*^eK}.$$
It maps $N_X(j_2^e)^*Ru_*^e j^e_{1!}L$ to $(j_2^p)^*Ru_*^p j^p_{1!}N_XL$. Using the specified composite in [def-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison], multiply the three identities already proved:
$$\begin{aligned}
\theta^p C_L
&=c^p\,Rp_*^p\bigl(e^p\,b_p^*E_{j_1}\,a_{b,K}\bigr)\,d_p(b_e^*K)\,N_X(r^e)\\
&=c^p\,Rp_*^p(E_sN_V(e^e))\,d_p(b_e^*K)\,N_X(r^e)\\
&=c^p\,Rp_*^p(E_s)\,d_p(s^e_!L)\,N_X(Rp_*^e(e^e))\,N_X(r^e)\\
&=N_X(c^e)\,N_X(Rp_*^e(e^e))\,N_X(r^e)=N_X(\theta^e).
\end{aligned}$$
The first line is (R) and naturality of $r^p$ in $E_{j_1}$; the second is (O); the third is naturality of $d_p$ in $e^e$; the fourth is (C). This explicitly compares the three constituents defining the two theta maps.

source.place: Tag 0F7B, lemma-shriek-proper-and-open, refinement case; explicit three-constituent calculation

proof.text: Let $H=Ru_*^p(E_{j_1}(L))\,d_u(K)\,N_{T_2}(\alpha^e_{u,L})$. Transport its source by $E_{j_2}(L)^{-1}$, obtaining a map from $j^p_{2!}N_XL$. Under the open adjunction [prop-exc-open-adjoint], its transpose is $C_LN_X((\theta^e)^{-1})$: this follows by naturality of $a_{j_2}$ and the open-unit compatibility of $E_{j_2}$ established in Step 5, since the transpose of $\alpha^e$ is $(\theta^e)^{-1}$ by [def-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison]. Step 10 makes this transpose $(\theta^p)^{-1}$. By definition this is also the transpose of $\alpha^p_{u,R}(N_XL)$. Injectivity of the open-adjunction hom bijection gives $H=\alpha^p_{u,R}(N_XL)E_{j_2}(L)$, the required site equation. Every factor and every hom bijection used is natural in $L$, so both equations are natural. The only cartesian squares used are those defining $V$ and open base change inside $V$; the original refinement square was never assumed cartesian. The coefficient argument used just the two stated lower bounds and imposed no flatness on $B$.

source.place: Tag 09AF, lemma-jshriek-comparison; open-adjunction transpose of the three-constituent identity
